verdict.rationale: GitBook documents a CLI for shell-based work: listing organizations, inspecting spaces and pages, asking questions against docs, and building and publishing integrations. It also offers a RESTful API and Git Sync, so docs can be automated without the UI. However, nothing shows CI pipeline usage specifically, and the CLI's described scope centers on inspection and integrations rather than end-to-end content publishing. A community note says the legacy CLI is no longer under active development; that refers to the old open-source tool, not the currently documented CLI. Missing for 10: documented CI/CD integration (e.g. GitHub Actions or tokens for non-interactive runs), CLI coverage of content publishing and updates, independent hands-on corroboration of headless automation.
